question: None shared. P-92 is binary MCI vs NC from a DTI + rs-fMRI connectome GCN (ADNI, 116 NC / 98 MCI). P-97 is 4-class HC / EMCI / LMCI / AD staging from rs-fMRI-only connectivity embeddings (ADNI, 125 subjects). The channel is shared (MRI), but the comparison is not: 2 classes against 4 stages including AD. P-97 reports no binary MCI-vs-HC figure of its own; the two-class results in its Table 2 are other studies'.
metric: Mismatch: binary accuracy (P-92, Best column 92.7%, average 86.3%) against 4-class accuracy and quadratic kappa averaged over 100 repeats of 5-fold CV (P-97, 97.73%). Neither paper reports an AUC, although the record gives both an AUC (91% and 89%).

figures.P-92: MCI vs NC, 5-fold CV, n = 214: accuracy Best 92.7 / Worst 83.3 / Average 86.3 (Table 4, best setting); second ADNI subset (124) Best 94.1 / Average 92.0. No AUC.
figures.P-97: 4-class HC/EMCI/LMCI/AD, 5-fold CV repeated 100 times, n = 125: accuracy 97.73% (SVM) / 97.32% (LR), quadratic kappa 96.86% / 96.74%; without the mapping function 87.2% / 86.96%. No AUC.

matched_figure_check: Not applicable: no shared contrast. Neither paper reports a result under the other's condition (P-92 has no 4-class result; P-97 has no binary MCI-vs-HC result).
performance_validity: P-97 meets the Section 3.5 exclusion: 97.73% accuracy on internal CV only, 125 subjects over four classes, no external cohort. P-92 (Best 92.7%, average 86.3%) does not.
reason: The papers classify different contrasts: binary MCI vs NC against 4-class staging with AD. Their accuracy summaries are not the same quantity, and P-97's 97.73% meets the performance-validity exclusion. The recorded pair (GCN 91% AUC vs DTI + rs-fMRI concatenation 89% AUC on the same validation set) misreads both papers: neither reports an AUC, P-97 uses no DTI, and the samples differ. The record itself calls the gap marginal.
